solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put on make-up for comedy

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing put on another comes after it, so the word for put follows the word for make-up

parts.note: slap is theatrical slang for greasepaint or cosmetics
to stick something somewhere is to put it there

explanation.surface: An actor applies greasepaint before going on stage in a comic role.
explanation.walkthrough: SLAP is British slang for make-up; 'Put on' reads as one phrase but splits, with 'Put' supplying letters and 'on' placing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical humour, a broad style of comic performance full of pratfalls.

clue.text: Line shoots up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from the bottom of the grid upwards

parts.note: to shoot a gun is to fire it

explanation.surface: A queue of people, or a row of guns, starts firing skywards.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography the small stroke finishing the end of a letter's main strokes is a short decorative line.

clue.text: In tour of Nevada ticket required — that's of benefit

indicators.note: the word for ticket is placed inside the reworked letters
a tour moves around, so the state's name is taken round and its letters rearranged

parts.note: the US state, taken as written to be rearranged
a tag is a label or ticket attached to goods

explanation.surface: A traveller touring Nevada is told that buying a ticket will pay off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tour' reads as a trip round the state, but it tells you to rearrange the state's name; the ticket goes in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage is a favourable circumstance or gain, the same idea as a benefit or profit.

clue.text: Asinine goat?

parts.note: asinine means foolish, like a donkey
a billy is a male goat

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a goat is also a fool, as in 'acting the goat', so a foolish goat describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly billy is an affectionate British name for a foolish person, someone behaving like a donkey or a clown.

clue.text: North is abroad, basically

indicators.note: abroad can mean all over the place or astray, so the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: both words taken as written, with the compass point spelt out in full

explanation.surface: Someone sums up a trip: the north of the country is essentially foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' is spelt out in full as fodder, not abbreviated: all five letters join IS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a summary, meaning to put things briefly or at the most fundamental level.

clue.text: Tackle figures producing litter

definitions.note: the answer is plural; a litter is a group of them

parts.note: tackle is gear or equipment, as is kit
tens are numbers, figures

explanation.surface: Fishing gear and some numbers somehow generate rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish but means a brood of young animals born together.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat gives birth to a litter, a group of young born at one time, so the young cats make up that brood.

clue.text: Con prison warder

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cheat or swindle someone
second meaning: British prison slang for a jail officer

explanation.surface: An inmate and a guard, a convict next to a warder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' tempts as a noun for a convict beside the warder, but here it is the verb to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for both cheating someone out of something and for a prison officer guarding inmates.

clue.text: Lone swimmer

explanation.surface: A solitary person doing lengths in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means only or single, and is also a flat sea fish, a crossword favourite for swimmer.

clue.text: Just one way

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a direction, the opposite of left

explanation.surface: A road sign announcing a single permitted direction of traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes what is fair and proper, and also names a direction to turn, opposite to left.

clue.text: Critical moment when vital stuff abandoned

parts.note: water is essential to life
to shed something is to cast it off

explanation.surface: A crisis arrives when essential supplies are deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning point, an event after which things are never the same, as a ridge divides rainfall between river basins.

clue.text: Party in control moving to the left

indicators.note: in an across clue, travelling leftwards means reading the word from right to left

parts.note: a lever is a control, as on a machine

explanation.surface: A political party in power shifting its policies leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' reads as a political noun but is the verb to celebrate wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To party is to celebrate with lively festivity, which is what revelling means.

clue.text: Greek character welcomed by minor, excited

indicators.note: something welcomed by another is taken in by it, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: slight means small, minor
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A child gets excited at greeting a visitor from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' looks like a young person, but it is the adjective for slight.
explanation.definitionFit: To set someone alight is figuratively to fire them with enthusiasm, so the past form matches excited.

clue.text: Rich individual poking my dodgy bills

parts.note: 'that's rich' means that's laughable, so rich can mean amusing

indicators.note: something poking into another is pushed inside it

parts.note: taken as written
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A wealthy person poking through a pile of suspicious invoices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' looks like wealthy, but means amusing or absurd, as in 'that's rich!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterfeit or illicit cash is called funny money, and banknotes are bills in American usage.

clue.text: Leading source of light

definitions.note: the answer used as an adjective, as in a star player

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a luminous celestial body

explanation.surface: The principal origin of illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works attributively for the top performer in a cast, and names a sun shining in the night sky.

clue.text: Tie revolutionary up after prisoner in private chamber

indicators.note: the reversed part comes after the prisoner in the answer

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the words are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up
red is slang for a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A captive radical is bound and held in a secret cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both the tie and the revolutionary together, read bottom to top as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: A powder room is a euphemism for a ladies' toilet, a discreet room set aside for freshening up.

clue.text: Plan to orbit moon in vehicle

indicators.note: to orbit is to circle round, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A space agency maps out a lunar orbit by spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Io is one of Jupiter's large moons, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in ancient racing and war, a kind of conveyance.

clue.text: Primarily, calumny nastiest sort of malevolence

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of calumny

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variety of it, so the letters are sorted into another form

parts.note: taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Slander is, first and foremost, the meanest kind of spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattiness is spiteful, sly unkindness in speech, a petty form of ill will toward others.

clue.text: Put up with corporation

definitions.meaning: second meaning: old humorous British term for a pot belly

explanation.surface: Someone tolerating their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company, but is a jokey old word for a large paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach is to tolerate something unpleasant, and the noun is the belly, jokingly called a corporation.

clue.text: Machine, gold, red and brown at the bottom

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
tomato is a shade of red, and the fruit is the classic red thing

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of brown

explanation.surface: A list of colours, gold, red and brown, describing a piece of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The colour words mislead: gold is an element symbol, red stands for a red fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating mechanical device, often a figure moving like a robot.

clue.text: Order is about right for framework

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier words wrap round the letter for right

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A command that is roughly correct about a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' wants to be an anagram signal, but it is a verb supplying letters, and both first words together wrap round right.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice of crossed wooden or metal strips supporting climbing plants, a kind of open frame.

clue.text: Visible change around house

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a swing is a change, as in a swing in the polls
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: An obvious difference around the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something showing, such as a slip under a hem, can be seen, so it is in plain view.

clue.text: Husband having left, she saw boyfriend relaxed

indicators.note: the husband having left means his letter departs from the word beside it

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband
to date someone is to see them romantically

explanation.surface: After her husband walked out, she began seeing a new man and felt calmer.
explanation.walkthrough: H comes out of SHE, leaving SE, which is followed by DATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedated means calmed with a drug, so made tranquil or at ease.

clue.text: Republic promoting dope in mark of approval?

indicators.note: the first piece goes inside the mark of approval

parts.note: a seal of approval is an endorsement

indicators.note: promoting means raising, and in a down clue raising a word means reading it upwards

parts.note: dope and gen are both slang for information

explanation.surface: A government is endorsing drug use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs; it is slang for information, the same sense as 'give me the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a West African country with an elected president, a republic since independence from France.

clue.text: Measure bird, though not head

indicators.note: not the head means the word loses its front letter

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone measures a bird but leaves out its head.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a unit of length, an imperial measure of about two and a half centimetres.

clue.text: Good Lord, soldier royal companion

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like good lord
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a soldier escorting royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Elizabeth II famously kept these dogs, so a royal companion is a pet, not a courtier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh herding dog is famous as the late Queen's favourite pet, a constant royal friend.

clue.text: Noble army beaten by new compatriot

parts.note: a count is a nobleman

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's forces are defeated by a fresh enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A countryman can mean a person from one's own nation, a fellow citizen of the same land.

clue.text: More pleasing part of volcanic eruption

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters are a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A lava flow is the more agreeable bit of an eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, meaning more agreeable or delightful.

clue.text: Crack picture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an attempt, as in have a crack at it

explanation.surface: An expert photograph, as in a crack photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an attempt at something and also a photograph taken with a camera.

clue.text: Human alerting alien about explosive gas

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the gas
alien means strange or foreign, so the letters are made unfamiliar by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written to be rearranged
H is the symbol for hydrogen, a highly explosive gas

explanation.surface: A person warning an extraterrestrial about a dangerous gas leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' looks like the creature in the scene, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthling is what science fiction aliens call a person, an inhabitant of our planet.

clue.text: Work on mannerism of a looker

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tic is a habitual twitch or quirk

explanation.surface: Practising the characteristic quirk of a beautiful person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A looker' suggests an attractive person, but means something that looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an old or humorous word for an eye, the organ we look with.

clue.text: Change working hours

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a scheduled period of work

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter a work schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to move or alter, and also a block of time a worker is rostered on duty.

clue.text: Dig more land, missing two bits, one searching for buried treasure

indicators.note: digging turns soil over, which is the setter's hint that the letters are churned up
missing two bits means a pair of letters drop out of the fodder

parts.note: the words taken as written, before two letters are lost

explanation.surface: A prospector excavates more ground despite losing some equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The two lost bits are the A and D of LAND; the remaining DIG MORE LN is then rearranged. The anagram signal is barely there, so the definition and crossers carry it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold miner digs for precious ore hidden underground, a prospector after buried riches.
